chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: Benny Goodman's influence and the swing feel
summary: Mundy moved the band toward swing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Did the success of -- speaking of Goodman, did his success in the mid-thirties, did that have an effect on Grand Terrace business? Did it have an effect on what you guys played, or anything, that popularity? Of course there'd been that music played all along.

Well, we changed the swing. We started playing different type of music. Started playing Benny Goodman type music, which was swing, which was easy because we had Jimmy Mundy. He started us playing swing.
What was the difference between that and what you'd been doing before?
Well, it was more subdued type of jazz, you know. Had a different beat.
Can you explain what the difference
It's hard. It's hard to explain the difference.
Yeah, well, I know what the difference is, but -- well, one, it flowed.
Went like that, instead of this.
Right, right. But that was an important change in the music, the rhythm section.
The rhythm section was changing. Of course, when guitars, you know, instead of banjos came in, that helped that flow also, I think.
